pr_title: [4.x] Fix locale resource remapping with binary conversion on export
pr_body:
This fixes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/63606 for Godot 4.x

I made the Godot 3.x version first, which is PR https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/63629

This is essentially the same fix as the Godot 3.x one, just cherry-picked and with the conflicts resolved.

As I noted there:

> I have no idea if this is the right fix, but it works and seems to make sense. The previous `if (new_path == p_path) {` seems to be checking if the `path_remap` had anything, so replacing that with an `else` allows the .remap files to get used even when there was a locale remap.
pr_comments: Added comment based on one suggested by reduz on RocketChat!

issue_context.title: Remapped (localized) resources fail to load with "Convert Text Resources To Binary On Export" enabled
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

3.4.4-stable

### System information

Linux, GLES3, 1070M

### Issue description

I've been translating Retro Tank Party into a number of languages, including a couple "non-alphabet" languages like Japanese and Chinese. In order to accommodate them, I needed switch to a different font when in those languages.

The "Localization" -> "Remap" feature in Project Settings is a great fit for this! But I couldn't just remap the .ttf file, because the two fonts are sized a little differently, so I saved a `DynamicFont` resource as a .tres, and remapped that to a different .tres when necessary, so they could have different "font_data" and a different "size"

This works great when running the game in the editor!

However, when I export the game (with "Convert Text Resources To Binary On Export" enabled), the remapped font fails to load and I get errors like this (from my MRP project below):

```
ERROR: Cannot open file 'res://monogram_extended.tres'.
   at: load_interactive (scene/resources/resource_format_text.cpp:1183)
ERROR: Failed loading resource: res://monogram_extended.tres. Make sure resources have been imported by opening the project in the editor at least once.
   at: _load (core/io/resource_loader.cpp:270)
ERROR: Can't load dependency: res://monogram.tres.
   at: poll (core/io/resource_format_binary.cpp:611)
ERROR: Failed to load resource 'res://Main.tscn.converted.res'.
   at: load (core/io/resource_loader.cpp:206)
ERROR: Failed loading resource: res://Main.tscn.converted.res. Make sure resources have been imported by opening the project in the editor at least once.
   at: _load (core/io/resource_loader.cpp:270)
ERROR: Failed loading scene: res://Main.tscn
   at: start (main/main.cpp:2011)
```

It fails to load the binary version of the resource. In fact, it appears as though it's still trying to load the text version as the first error comes from resource_format_text.cpp.

If I disable "Convert Text Resources To Binary On Export", then the exported version works fine.

~~This is all Godot 3.x - I haven't had a chance to test if this bug is present in Godot 4 as well.~~

**UPDATE: I just tested this in Godot 4.x and the bug is present there too!**

### Steps to reproduce

There's quite a few steps to reproduce (using the MRP below is probably easier) but I'll give the high-level version:

1. Create two `DynamicFont` (Godot 3.x) or `LabelSettings` (Godot 4.x) resources with different TTF fonts in their "font_data" and save them as .tres files (for example, monogram.tres and monogram_extended.tres like in the MRP)
2. Make a scene (which'll be the main scene for the project) with a `Label` that uses the first font (say, monogram.tres) as the font under "Theme Overrides" (Godot 3.x) or "Label Settings" (Godot 4.x)
3. In "Project Settings" in the "Localization" -> "Remaps" tab, add the first font (ex. monogram.tres) under Resources, and add the second font (ex. monogram_extended.ttf) as a remap under "Remaps by Locale" for some non-English locale (ex. Polish)
4. In "Project Settings" in the "General" tab, set "Locale" -> "Test" to the locale code for the non-English locale used in the previous step (ex. "pl")
4. Also in the "General" tab, enable "Editor" -> "Convert Text Resources To Binary On Export"
5. If you run the game in the editor, everything will work fine! (Doing this at this point is a good idea, because you'll be prompted to set a main scene)
6. Setup an export for your platform, export and then run it - it will not work fine. :-) In the MRP, the game crashes after the Godot splash screen, and gives the errors messages above

As a workaround, if I make an autoload singleton that loads the first font resource (ex monogram.tres) in its `_ready()` method, then everything works fine. I think it's because directly loading the individual font resource does the correct remapping, and once the resource is loaded, that will just be reused when loading the scene. It's when the font is loaded as part of a scene (and the font resource isn't already loaded) that the problem happens for some reason.

### Minimal reproduction project

Godot 3.x: [FontRemapTest.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/9215711/FontRemapTest.zip)

Godot 4.x: [FontRemapTest4x.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/9221466/FontRemapTest4x.zip)

The MRP is a little bit more sophisticated than the "Steps to reproduce". I also setup English and Polish translations, so the text in the label would be different for the two different locales, and I made sure to use characters in Polish that are only present in the remapped font (monogram_extended.ttf). So, it's a little more realistic, but this little extra stuff isn't necessary to make the bug happen.
comments: I just tested Godot 4.x (using the latest 'master') and I confirmed that this problem is present in Godot 4 as well! I've updated the issue description with this information, and uploaded an MRP for Godot 4 (following the same high-level steps to reproduce as the Godot 3.x version).

review_comments: The thing here is that new_path may have been changed earlier in the function due to a translation remap.
